source_boundary.preserved_question_intent: Explain the four InnoDB transaction isolation levels and identify the default level, with enough mechanism detail to distinguish READ COMMITTED and REPEATABLE READ without turning the answer into a generic ANSI anomaly table detached from MySQL behavior.

sources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual 17.7.2.1 Transaction Isolation Levels
anchors: InnoDB supports READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE
READ COMMITTED creates a fresh snapshot for each consistent read
REPEATABLE READ consistent reads in one transaction use the snapshot established by the first consistent read
REPEATABLE READ locking/range operations use record/gap/next-key locking depending on the search condition
SERIALIZABLE is like REPEATABLE READ but may convert plain SELECT to SELECT FOR SHARE when autocommit is disabled

sources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual 7.1.8 transaction_isolation system variable
anchors: valid values are READ-UNCOMMITTED, READ-COMMITTED, REPEATABLE-READ and SERIALIZABLE
transaction isolation can be assigned at global/session/next-transaction scopes

sources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual 17.7.2.3 Consistent Nonlocking Reads
anchors: InnoDB consistent reads use multi-versioning to present a snapshot
REPEATABLE READ ordinary consistent SELECT statements reuse the first consistent-read snapshot in a transaction
READ COMMITTED ordinary consistent SELECT statements create a fresh snapshot for each read
consistent nonlocking reads do not set row locks and are distinct from locking reads

sources.title: MySQL 8.4 Reference Manual 17.7.2.4 Locking Reads
anchors: SELECT FOR SHARE and SELECT FOR UPDATE are locking reads
locking reads reserve rows against concurrent modification until commit or rollback
locking-read behavior must not be conflated with ordinary consistent snapshot SELECT behavior

claims.text: InnoDB supports READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE. Its default transaction isolation level is REPEATABLE READ.

At READ UNCOMMITTED, ordinary SELECT can observe an earlier/uncommitted row version and reads are not consistent; this is the dirty-read level and otherwise behaves similarly to READ COMMITTED in the InnoDB description.
At READ COMMITTED, each consistent nonlocking read creates and reads a fresh snapshot, so two ordinary SELECT statements in the same transaction need not see the same committed database state.

At the default REPEATABLE READ level, consistent nonlocking reads in one transaction use the snapshot established by the first consistent read. Locking reads and DML are a different access path and can use record/gap/next-key locking for ranges, so the answer must distinguish snapshot reads from locking reads instead of reducing MySQL RR to a one-line anomaly table.

SERIALIZABLE is stricter than REPEATABLE READ; with autocommit disabled, InnoDB implicitly converts plain SELECT to SELECT FOR SHARE, increasing locking/serialization behavior and reducing concurrency.

The transaction isolation setting can be configured globally, per session, or for the next transaction, so the interview default should be stated as the InnoDB/server default rather than assuming every application connection necessarily uses it unchanged.

writer_constraints: Answer all three frozen source variants, including the default isolation level: REPEATABLE READ for InnoDB/MySQL's default transaction_isolation setting.
Name all four levels and explain them in increasing isolation order.
Use MySQL/InnoDB behavior, not only the textbook SQL-92 anomaly matrix. In particular, explain RC fresh-snapshot-per-consistent-read versus RR first-consistent-read snapshot reuse.
Keep ordinary consistent SELECT separate from SELECT FOR UPDATE/FOR SHARE and DML; MySQL RR locking behavior uses record/gap/next-key locks depending on the access path.
Do not state that RR universally prevents every possible form of phantom in every read/write pattern. Explain snapshot consistency and locking-read range protection precisely.
Do not claim isolation level alone solves all application concurrency anomalies such as lost updates; read-modify-write correctness also depends on locking/conditional updates/application protocol.
Mention that isolation can be changed per global/session/next transaction so 'default RR' is not proof of a given connection's current setting.
Do not fabricate production benchmarks or personal experience.
